merged_findings.item: 4. SYNTHESIS — does the high-speed/low-speed split hold, and the waggle-dance blur
merged_findings.claim: The two-channel (latency) organization is a robust ORGANIZING distinction the literature SUPPORTS but does not itself name as a binary — the channels differ in latency by ~2-4 orders of magnitude. It BLURS at the edges, most sharply at the honeybee WAGGLE DANCE: a high-speed, direct, point-to-small-group channel (a dancer signals a handful of followers in real time; ~75 ms per ~100 m; direction via angle-to-gravity/sun-azimuth; ~2.5 s waggle run ~ 2,625 m) that nonetheless ENCODES PERSISTENT SPATIAL map-content (a vector to a distant resource). The dance is PERSISTENT in information-TYPE but TRANSIENT in MECHANISM (it is not stored in the environment; the dancer relies on internal memory). So a fast channel carries map-like content a stigmergic field would otherwise hold. Vibrational signals (stop-signal, DVAV; Seeley et al. 2012 cross-inhibition) further blur it by MODULATING slower collective decisions. The split is by LATENCY (transient direct contact vs persistent environmental store), NOT by information-type. Apis mellifera notably uses the waggle dance + volatile recruitment rather than trail pheromones (which stingless bees, Meliponini, do use), reducing its stigmergic-channel role. Riley et al. (2005, Nature 435:205-207) experimentally confirmed the dance-vector via harmonic-radar flight tracking (DOI confirmed via search, not direct-fetched this pass).
merged_findings.best_citation: Waggle-dance encoding: von Frisch, K. (1967). The Dance Language and Orientation of Bees. Belknap/Harvard Univ. Press (canonical reference). Experimental confirmation: Riley, J.R. et al. (2005). The flight paths of honeybees recruited by the waggle dance. Nature 435:205-207, DOI 10.1038/nature03526 (search-confirmed, not direct-fetched — FLAG). Cross-inhibition coupling fast signals to decisions: Seeley, T.D. et al. (2012). Science 335(6064):108-111.

merged_findings.item: 4. SYNTHESIS — ranking the three taxa by clean latency separation [LENS / researcher imposition]
merged_findings.claim: Ranking by how CLEANLY the two channels separate by latency (cleanest first): (1) TERMITES — fast = substrate-borne vibrational drumming (sub-second response, relay at ~1.3-2.1 m/s); slow = the constructed mound/nest (the founding stigmergy case), persisting the colony lifetime; little fast-channel-carrying-a-spatial-map confound (BUT termite trail/construction-pheromone persistence is less precisely quantified in directly-verified sources than for ants — a caveat). (2) ANTS — clean but with overlap; fast = antennation/trophallaxis/contact-alarm (~1.51 s); slow = trail-pheromone field (half-life 3-47 min) + CHC identity field as external memory; the most QUANTIFIED stigmergic dynamics (Deneubourg-Goss). (3) HONEY BEES — most BLURRED: the waggle dance is a fast channel carrying persistent spatial content, and stop/vibration signals modulate slow decisions. FLAG: this cross-taxon ranking is the RESEARCHER'S SYNTHESIS/imposition; NO cited author presents such an explicit ordering, and the literature is effectively silent on a formal cross-taxon comparison of channel-latency cleanliness. Both surveys independently produced the SAME ranking, but it remains a lens, not a literature claim.

merged_result.cross_cutting:
MERGE METHOD: union of both surveys (15 opus + 18 sonnet findings) collapsed to 18 merged items, no model privileged. Where the surveys overlapped I kept the best-attested claim + citation; sonnet-only findings (Greenwald 2015 trophallactic networks, Guo 2022 ant alarm propagation, Tan 2016 stop-signal, Deneubourg-Goss reinforcement, Choe 2018 termite royal pheromone, Canciani-Arnellos-Moreno 2019, niche construction) were pulled in for coverage; opus served as the citation-discipline spine (tighter verified/not-reverified separation; honest verified:false on the weak alarm-pheromone item).

TERMINOLOGY (verified consistent with the cited literature): 'colony'/'superorganism' = the distributed organismal unit across ants, termites, honey bees; 'hive' = the honey-bee NEST structure specifically, never the organism and not used for ants/termites.

TWO-CHANNEL ORGANIZATION (the spine), stated as a latency partition the literature SUPPORTS but does not itself name as a binary, differing by ~2-4 orders of magnitude: (A) HIGH-SPEED / DIRECT / POINT-TO-POINT, sub-second-to-seconds, transient, between adjacent (air-gapped) bodies — antennation (19.5-41.5 strikes/s), trophallaxis (seconds-to-minutes; JH/protein/miRNA payload), substrate-borne vibration (termite drumming relay; bee stop-signal 302-550 Hz/150-258 ms & DVAV), contact-mediated alarm (~1.51 s), fast volatile alarm pheromone. Reciprocity grades from CLOSED-LOOP/answered (bee stop-signal halts a specific dancer; termite drumming relayed by receivers) through mutual-assay (antennation, trophallaxis dyad) to ONE-WAY release-and-amplify (alarm pheromone). (B) LOW-SPEED / INDIRECT / STIGMERGIC, minutes-to-hours-to-colony-lifetime, broadcast one-to-many across time, mediated by the SHARED ENVIRONMENT — trail-pheromone fields (half-life 3-47 min, species/substrate dependent; written by deposition, read by following, reinforced by traffic, decay = forgetting), the built nest/mound (Grasse's founding stigmergy case), and the queen-pheromone / CHC colony-identity field (writable into and re-readable from nest material).

THE LOAD-BEARING QUESTION resolves AFFIRMATIVELY at the MECHANISM level: stigmergy IS treated as externalized, environmentally-stored memory. The mechanism (one agent writes into the medium, another reads it back later) is established (Grasse 1959; Theraulaz & Bonabeau 1999; Bonabeau-Dorigo-Theraulaz 1999). Hunt, Franks & Baddeley (2020) make it operational ('store the information externally in the environment'; 'external memory store'; measured p=0.0161). 'Collective/external/stigmergic memory' is ESTABLISHED operationally-defined usage in that primary source; 'extended cognition/extended mind' (Clark & Chalmers 1998) and niche-construction 'ecological inheritance' (Odling-Smee 2003) are the more METAPHORICAL/contested extensions, NOT technical terms in Grasse or Theraulaz & Bonabeau.

SUPERORGANISM STATUS: widely USED heuristic, CONTESTED as a strict entity-level evolutionary claim — Wheeler 1911 origin; Hoelldobler & Wilson 2009 synthesis; Gardner & Grafen 2009 formal limits; Boomsma & Gawne 2018 restriction to irreversible-caste 'points of no return'; Canciani-Arnellos-Moreno 2019 organizational critique; the kin-vs-multilevel-selection controversy (Nowak-Tarnita-Wilson 2010 + 130-author rebuttal) is the backdrop (it concerns the ORIGIN of eusociality, not the descriptive framing).

THE SPLIT BLURS, primarily at the honeybee waggle dance — a FAST direct channel encoding PERSISTENT spatial map-content (~75 ms/100 m; angle-to-gravity) — PERSISTENT in information-type, TRANSIENT in mechanism. The partition is by LATENCY (transient direct edge vs persistent environmental store), NOT by information-type. Cleanest-to-blurriest latency separation: termites > ants > honey bees — BOTH surveys independently produced this same ordering, but it is the RESEARCHER'S SYNTHESIS, not any cited author's explicit claim (the literature is silent on a formal cross-taxon comparison).
